parsed.reason: The message owns the failure cleanly on Hale's end ("didn't work on my end"), uses first-person language, and clearly states nothing was changed ("your week is still as it was"). It avoids technical jargon, apologies, and any implication that the parent needs to do something. "Your week" correctly refers to the family's schedule, not a place to visit. The tone is direct and competent—a friend acknowledging they dropped something. Both required meanings are present: ownership and no change.
